Risk-based approach: standard CDD where AML/CFT risk is low and enhanced CDD where AML/CFT risk is high pursuant to Sections 9 and 9A.

Section 5(1) requires FIs and DNFBPs to undertake CDD when:
- establishing business relations with a customer.
- carrying out transactions above the prescribed amount, both singular transactions and multiple transactions that appear to be linked.
- carrying out wire transfers.
- there is suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing.
- there are doubts about the veracity and adequacy of previously obtained identification data.

column14:
Pursuant to Section 15, FIs and DNFBPs are required to promptly submit STRs to FIU where they suspect or have reasonable grounds to suspect that a transaction or attempted transaction involving property is related or linked to a serious offence or a money laundering offence. 

This also include special rules applied to advocates, solicitors, notaries, other independent legal professionals and accountants. These professionals are required to submit STRs only when they engage, on behalf of or for a client, in specified financial or corporate activities, such as buying or selling real estate, managing client money or assets, managing bank or securities accounts, or creating, operating or managing legal persons or arrangements. They are not required to report information obtained in the course of ascertaining a client’s legal position or defending or representing a client in judicial, administrative, arbitration or mediation proceedings, provided the services are not being used to facilitate illegal activity. Failure to comply with STR obligations, or breaching the tipping‑off prohibition, constitutes a serious offence under the legislation.
column15:
Pursuant to Section 16, FIs and DNFBPs as well as dealers in high value goods are required to submit Cash Transaction Reports (CTRs) to the FIU for any currency transaction equal to or exceeding the prescribed amount. This requirement applies to transactions conducted as a single transaction or as several transactions that appear to be linked, and also applies to attempted transactions.

Cash transaction reports must be submitted promptly and no later than five working days after the transaction or attempted transaction occurs, in the manner and form prescribed. Failure to submit a required cash transaction report constitutes an offence under the Order.
column16:
Pursuant to Section 6A (1), all wire transfers shall be accompanied with the following information:
- full name of the originator
- originator's account number, or in the absence of an account number, a unique transaction reference number
- originator's address or national identity number or customer identification number or date and place of birth
- name of the beneficiary
- beneficiary's account number, or in the absence of an account number, a unique transaction reference number
column18:
Section 22(d) requires FIs and DNFBPs to have in place policies and procedures to identify and assess the risks of ML/TF resulting from the development of new products and business practices, including new delivery mechanisms and the use of new or developing technologies for new and pre-existing products by:
- conducting risk assessment prior to the launch and usage of such products, business practices and technologies; and
- taking appropriate measures to manage and mitigate such risks.

Section 22(da) requires FIs and DNFBPs to have in place adequate AML/CFT measures to identify, assess and understand the risks of ML/TF posted by its customers and beneficial owners, including if they are politically-exposed persons, the countries where they are from or the countries where they have operations, and their products and services –
- documenting the risk assessments;
- considering all the relevant risks factors before determining the level of overall risk and the appropriate type and extent of mitigation measures to be applied;
- keeping the risk assessments up-to-date; and
- having the mechanisms to provide the risk assessment information to the Authority.
column19:
Pursuant to Section 34, the FIU may:
- share information with any foreign counterpart agency that performs similar functions based upon reciprocity or mutual agreement on the basis of cooperation arrangements entered into between the FIU and such foreign counterpart agency;
- liaise with or enter into any agreement or arrangement with any international organisation regarding the exchange of information pursuant to this Order and disclose any report or information derived from such report to any international organisation in accordance with this Order;
- make inquiries on behalf of a foreign counterpart agency where the inquiry may be relevant to the foreign counterpart agency's analysis of a matter involving the investigation or prosecution of a money laundering offence or serious offence; and
- exchange feedback with a foreign counterpart agency on the use and usefulness of the information that was exchanged.

- Party to key international conventions, including the Vienna Convention, Palermo Convention, and UNCAC.
- Member of the Egmont Group and Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG)

column7:
Risk-based approach: simplified CDD where AML/CFT risk is low and enhanced CDD where AML/CFT risk is high

To be undertaken:
- prior to establishing business relations
- prior to carrying out occasional or one-off transactions, including wire transfers
- if the reporting entity has a suspicion of money laundering and/or financing of terrorism irrespective of the sum involved in the transaction
- if the reporting entity has any doubts about the veracity or adequacy of previously obtained customer identification data

Thresholds for undertaking CDD:
- occasional or one-off transactions: 40 million Riels
- remittance and wire transfers: 4 million Riels
- dealers in precious metals, stones and gem: 60 million Riels
- casinos and other gambling institutions: 12 million Riels

Enhanced due diligence requirements apply. In addition to the CDD measures -

For foreign PEPs, family members and close associates:
- obtain senior management approval before establishing (or continuing, for existing customers) the relationship
- take reasonable measures to establish the source of funds and wealth of such persons and beneficial owners identified as PEPs
- ensure that enhanced, ongoing monitoring is conducted on that relationship
- put risk management systems in place to identify customers or beneficial owners who are foreign PEPs

For domestic or international PEPs, family members and close associates
- take reasonable measures to determine whether a customer or beneficial owner is a domestic or international PEP
- apply enhanced, ongoing monitoring where a customer is identified as a domestic or international PEPs and the relationship is assessed as a higher risk relationship

Risk-based approach: simplified CDD where AML/CFT risk is low and enhanced CDD where AML/CFT risk is high

To be undertaken when:
- establishing business relations
- providing money-changing and wholesale currency (simplified for transactions amounting to RM3,000 to RM10,000; standard CDD for transactions amounting to RM10,000 and above)
- providing wire transfer services (simplified for transactions below RM3,000; standard CDD for transactions amounting to RM3,000 and above)
- providing e-money 
(i) simplified CDD for account limits below RM3,000 and used for domestic wire transfers
(ii) simplified CDD for account limits between RM3,000 and RM 4,999 when all the following conditions are met: monthly transaction is below RM5,000; annual transaction is below RM60,000; account is used for payments of goods and/or services within Malaysia only; account is used for domestic wire transfers; and cash withdrawal or cross-border wire transfers are not permitted
(iii) standard CDD when any of the following conditions are met: account limit is RM5,000 and above; monthly transaction is equivalent to RM5,000 and above; annual transaction is equivalent to RM60,000 and above; account is for payments of goods and/or services outside Malaysia; account is for cross-border wire transfers; or account is used for cash withdrawal
- carrying out occasional transactions involving an amount equivalent to RM25,000 and above, including in situations where the transaction is carried out in a single transaction or through several transactionsin a day that appear to be linked
- carrying out cash transactions involving an amount equivalent to RM25,000 and above
- there is any suspicion of ML/TF/PF, regardless of amount
- there is reasonable doubt about the veracity or adequacy of previously obtained information

(i) source of wealth and source of funds

- Senior management (HO) approvalbefore establishing (or continuinung, for existing customer) business relationship
column10:
- Gather sufficient information about a respondent institution to understand the nature of the respondent's business
- Assess AML/CFT/CPF controls implemented by the respondent institution having regard to AML/CFT/CPF measures of the country of jurisdiction in which the respondent institution operates
- Based on publicly available information, evaluate the reputation of the respondent institution and the quality of supervision to which it is subject, including whether it has been subject to a ML/TF/PF investigation or regulatory action
- Obtain approval from senior management before establishing new correspondent banking relationships
- Clearly understand the respective AML/CFT/CPF responsibilities of each institution
- With respect to "payable-through accounts", be satisfied that the respondent banks have performed CDD obligations on customers with direct access to the accounts and that respondents can provide relevant CDD information upon request
- Cease business relations with respondent banks that have relations or transactions with shell banks or allow their accounts to be used by shell banks
column11:
- Ultimate responsibility and accountability for CDD measures remains with the reporting institution
- Prohibition from relying on third parties located in higher risk countries 
- Prohibition from relying on third parties to conduct ongoing due diligence 
- Governed by an arrangement that clearly specifies the rights, responsibilities and expectations of all parties
- Attestation from the third party:
(i) has an adequate CDD process
(ii) has measures in place for record keeping requirements
(iii) can provide the CDD information and provide copies of the relevant documentation immediately upon request
(iv) is properly regulated and subjected to AML/CFT/CPF supervision by the relevant supervisory authority
column12:
- Scrutinize transactions undertaken throughout the course
of the relationship to ensure that the transactions being
conducted are consistent with the reporting institution’s
knowledge of the customer, their business and risk profile,
including where necessary, the source of funds
- Ensure that documents, data or information collected
under the CDD process is kept up-to-date and relevant, by
undertaking reviews of existing records particularly for
higher risk customers.
- Consider the economic background and purpose of
any transaction or business relationship which:
(a) appears unusual;
(b) is inconsistent with the expected type of activity and
business model when compared to the volume of
transaction;
(c) does not have any apparent economic purpose; or
(d) casts doubt on the legality of such transactions, especially
with regard to complex and large transactions or involving
higher risk customers.
column13:
- At least six years following the completion of the transaction, the termination of the business relationship or after the date of the occasional transaction
- Beyond six years in situations where the records are subjected to ongoing investigation or prosecution in court, until such time reporting institutions are informed by the relevant law enforcement agency that the records are no longer required
column14:
- Report to the Financial Intelligence and Enforcement Department of BNM within the next working day from the date the Compliance Officer establishes suspicion 
- Prohibition against tipping off
column15:
- Report to the Financial Intelligence and Enforcement Department of BNM within five working days from the date of transaction, single or multiple cash transactions within the same account in a day for the amount equivalent to RM25,000 and above

- No offsetting of cash transactions against one another (e.g., aggregate deposit and withdrawal transactions)
column16:
- Ensure that the message or payment instruction for all cross-border wire transfers involving an amount equivalent to RM3,000 and above are accompanied by the following:
(i) name of originator
(ii) originator's account number (or a unique reference number if there is no account number) which permits traceability of the transaction
(iii) address or date and place of birth of the originator
(iv) name of beneficiary
(v) beneficiary's account number (or a unique reference number if there is no account number) which permits traceability of the transaction

- Where several individual cross-border wire transfers from a single originator are bundled in a batch file for transmission to beneficiaries, only the originator's account number or unique transaction reference number of the transaction is necessary, so long as the batch file contains the required originator and full beneficiary information that is fully traceable within the beneficiary country

- Message or payment instruction for all cross-border wire transfers below RM3,000 shall be accompanied by the following information:
(i) name of originator and beneficiary
(ii) account number of the originator and beneficiary (or a unique reference number if there is no account number), which permits traceability of the transaction
column17:
- AML/CFT/CPF programme
- Procedures to ensure high standards of integrity of employees and system to evaluate the personal, employment and financial history of employees upon hiring the employee and throughout the course of employment
- Ongoing employee training and awareness programs
- Independent audit function to check compliance 
- Designation of compliance officers at management level to be reported to BNM within ten working working days from appoinment or change in appointment
- Reporting system for the submission of cash threshold and suspiciours transaction reports
- Management information system (manual or electronic) that would enable the detection of irregularities and/or any suspicious activity
column18:
- Documented and updated institutional risk assessment to identify, assess and understand ML/TF/PF risks in relation to customers, countries or geographic areas, products, services, transactions or delivery channels, and other relevant risk factors.
- Additional assessment as and when required by BNM
- Enhanced measures to manage and mitigate the identified risks
- Consider the following in conducting risk assessments:
(i) susceptibility to key and emerging crimes as well as higher risk sectors identified in the National Risk Assessment 
(ii) necessity of enhancing AML/CFT Compliane Programme to ensure any areas of higher ML/TF risk are appropriately mitigated

- Customer risk profiling that considers:
(i) customer risk
(ii) country or geographical risk
(iii) products, services, transactions or delivery channels
(iv) any other information suggesting that the customer is of higher risk

- Conduct of risk assessment prior to the launch or use of new products and business practices, include new delivery mechanisms and use of new or developing technologies for both new and pre-existing products
column19:
- May enter into an agreement or arrangement, in writing, with the government or corresponding authority of a foreign State regarding the exchange of information that would be relevant to the investigation or the prosecution of a money laundering offense, a terrorism financing offense, a restricted activity financing offense, or an offense that is substantially similar to any of the offenses
- The corresponding foreign authority should give appropriate undertakings for protecting the confidentiality of anything communicated to it, and for controlling the use that will be made of it, including an undertaking that it will not be used as evidence in any other proceedings
- Record in writing the reasons for all decisions to communicate information
- Party to key international conventions, including the Vienna Convention, Palermo Convention, and UNCAC
- Member of the Egmont Group and Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG)
column20:
- Maintain updated and comprehensive sanctions database, including the UNSCR List and the Domestic List, that is easily accessible by its employees at the head office, branch, subsidiary and where relevant, to the outsourced service providers or agents
- Conduct sanctions screening on existing, potential or new customers against the Domestic List and UNSCR List 
- Immediate freezing of customer's funds and properties, or blocking of transactions (where applicable), upon determination and confirmation of a customer's identity as a specified entity and/or related parties
- Reject a potential customer when there is a positive name match
- Immediately report to the Financial Intelligence and Enforcement Department of BNM and Inspector General of Policy upon determination that they are in possession or in control of funds or properties of any specified entity and/or related party

column7:
Risk-based approach: simplified CDD where AML/CFT risk is low and enhanced CDD where AML/CFT risk is high

To be undertaken in the following cases:
- before carrying out a transaction or opening an account for a customer
- before carrying out a transaction for a customer who is not in an estbalished business relationship with the reporting organization, when the transaction involves an amount which equals or exceeds USD 15,000, whether conducted as a single transaction or several transactions that appear to be linked
- before carrying out a domestic or international wire or electronic transaction for a customer
- whenever doubts exist about the veracity or adequacy of previously obtained customer identification data
- whenever there is a suspicion of money laundering and financing of terrorism
column8:
- For natural persons: full name (including aliases), national registration card/citizen scrutiny card/passport, permanent and mailing address, date of birth, nationality, occupation, phone number, photo, name and account numbers of two introducers (existing account holders)

- For legal persons and legal arrangements: name of company, address of head office, full address (including phone, fax), certificate of incorporation/memorandum of association/article of association/ partnership agreement/trust deed, name and address of board of directors (including phone number), identification documents of directors/shareholders/partners/settlors/trustees/protection and beneficiaries, board resolution authorizing opening and operation of the account, authorization by board of directors to representatives for conducting financial transactions, identification documents of authorized representations

- For NGO: name of NGO, head office address, certificate of registration, constitution on the NGO, name and address of executive committee, telephone no., name and address of senior management, registered address (if different from principal place of business), executive committee's decision regarding opening of account, identification documents of directors/senior officers of the NGO, authorization for the operation of accounts, identification documents of authorized representatives

column11:
Reporting organizations may rely on a third party which has a capacity to perform the following elements:
- able to obtain all information without delay
- able to make avaiable identification data and other documents relating to CDD measures without delay upon request
- able to comply with AML/CFT requirements

Reporting organizations remain ultimately responsible for the identification and verification of customers.

Before entering into a relationship with a third party, consider the AML/CFT risk associated with the country in which the third party is based. If the third party is identified as high risk, review any customer relationships introduced by the third party and terminate the relationship with the third party intermediary.
column12:
- Adopt procedures to monitor on an ongoing basis customer transactions and the relationship with the customer
- Monitoring should include scrutiny of customer transactions to ensure that they are being conducted according to knowledge of the customer, the customer's commercial activities, the customer risk profile and, where necessary, the source of funds and wealth
- Monitoring shall also include predetermined limits on the amount and volume of transactions and type of transactions
column13:

- copies of transaction reports and other related documents: at least five years after the report was submitted to the FIU
- risk assessment and other underlying information: more than five years
column14:

column15:

column16:

1. Full name of the originator
2. Originator account number where such an account is used to process the transaction

4. Name of the recipient and the recipient account number where such an account is used to process the transaction

- If there is no account number, a unique reference number shall be specified for each transfer
- Where several individual cross-border wire or electronic transfers from a single originator are bundled in a batch file for transmission to beneficiaries, only the originator's account number or unique transaction reference number which permits traceability of the transaction is necessary, so long as the batch file contains the required originator and beneficiary information that is fully traceable within the beneficiary country
- Information shall be maintained and transmitted by the financial institutions acting as intermediaries in a chain of payments
column17:

- Insurance companies and pre-need companies

- Mutual funds, close-end investment companies, common trust funds, and other similar persons
- Other entities administering or otherwise dealing in currency, commodities or financial derivatives based thereon, valuable objects, cash substitutes and other similar monetary instruments

-  Company service providers that provide any of the following services to third parties: (i) acting as a formation agent of juridical persons; (ii) acting as (or arranging for another person to act as) a director or corporate secretary of a company, a partner of a partnership, or a similar position in relation to other juridical persons; (iii) providing a registered office, business address or accommodation, correspondence or administrative address for a company, a partnership or any other legal person or arrangement; and (iv) acting as (or arranging for another person to act as) a nominee shareholder for another person
- Persons who provide any of the following services: (i) managing of client money, securities or other assets; (ii) management of bank, savings or securities accounts; (iii) organization of contributions for the creation, operation or management of companies; and (iv) creation, operation or management of juridical persons or arrangements, and buying and selling business entities
- Casinos
- Real estate developers and brokers
- Offshore gaming operators and their service providers
column7:
Risk-based approach: 
- reduced CDD for potentially low-risk clients
- average CDD for clients posing normal risk
- EDD for higher-risk accounts

To be undertaken when:
- establishing business relations with any customer
- undertaking any occasional but relevant business transaction for any customer who has not otherwise established relations with the covered person, as follows:
(i) transaction with a value exceeding P100,000, except for money changing or remittance transactions
(ii) two or more transactions believed to be linked and with an aggregate value exceeding P100,000
(iii) in relation to remittance and money changing transactions, any transaction or two or more transactions believed to be linked, with an aggregate value exceeding P5,000
- there is suspicion of ML or TF
- there is doubt about the veracity or adequacy of previously obtained customer identification data
column8:
- For individuals: name of customer; PhilSys Card Number; date and place of birth; address; contact number or information; citizenship or nationality; specimen signature or biometric; name, address, date and place of birth, contact number or information and citizenship or nationality of the beneficiary or beneficial owner, whenever applicable; valid identification documents or other reliable, independent source documents, data or information

- Juridical persons: name of juridical person; name, address, citizenship or nationality of beneficial owner, if applicable, and authorized signatories; official address; contact numbers or information; nature of business; specimen signatures or biometrics of the authorized signatory; certificates of registration; secondary license or certificate of authority; articles of incorporation/partnership; latest general information sheet; resolution authorizing the signatory to sign on behalf of the entity; for entities registered outside the Philippines, similar documents and information authenticated by senior officer or designated officer of the entity in the country of registration, or by the Philippine Consulate, company register or notary public where the entities are registered

- For legal arrangement: name of legal arrangement and proof of existence; address and country of establishment; nature, purpose and objects of the legal arrangement; names of the settlor, trustee, trustor, protector (if any), beneficiary and any other natural person exercising ultimate effective control over the legal arrangement; description of the purpose/activities of the legal arrangement; expected use of the account; amount, number, type, purpose and frequency of the transaction expected
column9:
- Conduct of enhanced due diligence (EDD) for PEPs, their immediate family members and close associates, including:
(i) supporting information on the intended nature of the business relationship/source of funds/source of wealth
(ii) reasons for intended or performed transactions
(iii) list of companies where they are a stockholder, director, officer or authorized signatory
(iv) other relevant information available through public databases or the internet
- list of banks where the individual has maintained or is maintaining an account
- Senior management approval to commence or continue the business relationship/transaction with the customer
- Reasonable measures to establish the source of wealth and the source of funds of customers and beneficial owners identified as PEPs
- Conduct of enhanced ongoing monitoring of the relationship
column10:
- Conduct due diligence on the respondent bank and identify, understand and assess the ML/TF risks in correspondent banking relationships, considering among others:
(i) nature of the service to be provided
(ii) profile of the respondent bank
(iii) the respondent bank's operating environment, including quality of AML/CFT regime and regulatory framework of the jurisdiction that issued license to the respondent bank

- Obtain approval from senior management when establishing new correspondent relationships
- Clearly understand and document the respective AML/CFT responsibilities of each institution
- Prohibition from entering into, or continuing, correspondent banking relationships with shell banks 
- Measures to ensure that respondent banks do not permit their accounts to be used by shell banks
- Periodic due diligence reviews and sanction screening of CDD information on the respondent bank, its owners, directors, senior management and authorized signatories
- Develop appropriate transaction monitoring system that will enable understanding of the usual or expected activities of the respondent bank and detect any unusual or suspicious transaction pattern of activity that is inconsistent with the purpose of services provided to the respondent banks
column11:
- Ultimate responsibility for knowing the customer, keeping the identification documents, and managing attendant risks shall rest with the covered person
- Gather sufficient information about the third party and the group to which it belongs, and be satisfied that the third party is regulated, and supervised or monitored for, and has measures in place for compliance with CDD and record-keeping requirements
- Document the respective responsibilities of each institution
- Obtain approval from senior management at inception of relationship before relying on the third party

- For covered person counterparty: written sworn certification that the third party has conducted the prescribed customer identification procedures in accordance with the law and regulations and has in its custody all the minimum information and/or documents required to be obtained from the customer, and that the relying covered person has the ability to obtain identification documents from the third party upon request without delay

- For third party operating outside the Philippines: written sworn certification that the third party has conducted the prescribed customer identification procedures in accordance with the law and regulations and has in its custody all the minimum information and/or documents required to be obtained from the customer, that the relying covered person has the ability to obtain identification documents from the third party upon request without delay, and that the laws of the country where the third party is operating has equal or more stringent customer identification process requirement and that it has not been cited in violation thereof.
column12:
- Establish a system that will enable understanding of the
normal and reasonable account or business activity of customers to ensure that the customers’ accounts and transactions are consistent with their knowledge of the customers, and the latter’s commercial activities, risk profile, and source of funds and detect unusual or suspicious patterns of account activity
- Examine the background and purpose of all complex, unusually large transactions, all unusual patterns of transactions, which have no apparent economic or lawful purpose, and other transactions that may be considered
suspicious
column13:
- Retention for five (5) years from the date of transaction/ following closure of account or termination of business relationship
- Beyond 5 years for records of customers/ accounts subject of a case
- CTR/STR: at least 5 years from submission to AMLC
column14:
- Report to AMLC within five (5) working days of date of determination of the suspicious nature of the transaction, which determination should be made not exceeding ten (10) calendar days from the date of transaction
- Prohibition against tipping off
column15: - Report to AMLC within five (5) working days from occurrence  transactions in cash or other equivalent monetary instrument exceeding P500,000
column16:
- Cross-border and domestic fund/wire transfers and related message not exceeding P50,000 or its equivalent in foreign currency shall include that the following information throughout the payment chain:
(i) name of the originator
(ii) name of the beneficiary
(iii) account number of the originator and beneficiary, or in its absence, a unique reference number

- For cross-border and domestic fund/wire transfers and related message amounting to P50,000 or more, or its equivalent in foreign currency, the following information should be obtained and accompany the wire transfer:
(i) name of the originator
(ii) originator account number or a unique transaction reference number which permits traceability of the transaction
(iii) originator’s address, or national identity number, or customer
identification number, or date and place of birth
(iv) name of the beneficiary
(v) beneficiary  account number or unique transaction reference number which permits traceability of the transaction

- Where several individual cross-border wire or electronic transfers from a single originator are bundled in a batch file for transmission to beneficiaries, only the originator's account number or unique transaction reference number which permits traceability of the transaction is necessary, so long as the batch file contains the required originator and beneficiary information that is fully traceable within the beneficiary country

- Intermediary financial institutions shall ensure that all originator and beneficiary information that accompany a wire transfer are retained in the payment message
column17:
- Group-wide Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Prevention Program
- Independent compliance function, with AML compliance office who is at least at senior officer level
- Effective and continuous AML/CFT training program for all directors, and responsible officers and employees
- Adequate screening and recruitment process
- Independent internal audit with adequate audit program
- Adequate safeguards on the confidentiality and use of information exchanged, including safeguards to prevent tipping-off
- Mechanism to comply with freeze, bank inquiry and asset preservation orders
- Mechanism to comply with prohibitions from conducting transactions with designated persons and entities
- Monitoring and reporting tools appropriate for the institution's risk profile and business complexity, including system for flagging and monitoring suspicious and covered transactions
column18:
- Institutional risk assessment to identify, understand and assess ML/TF/PF and sanctions risks arising from customers, countries or geographic areas of operations and customers, products, services, transactions or delivery channels, that is updated/ conducted at least once every two (2) years, or as often as the Board or senior management may direct, depending on the level of risks identified in the previous risk assessment.

- Assessment of ML/TF/PF and sanctions risks that may arise in relation to the development of new products and new business practices, including new delivery mechanisms, and the use of new or developing technologies for both new and pre-existing products

- Appropriate measures to manage and mitigate the identified risks
column19:
- Principle of mutuality and reciprocity
- The AMLC may refuse to comply with any request for assistance where the action sought by the request contravenes any provision of the Constitution or the execution of a request is likely to prejudice the national interest of the Philippines unless there is a treaty between the Philippines and the requesting State relating to the provision of assistance in relation to money laundering offenses.
- A request for mutual assistance from a foreign State must (1) confirm that an investigation or prosecution is being conducted in respect of a money launderer named therein or that he has been convicted of any money laundering offense; (2) state the grounds on which any person is being investigated or prosecuted for money laundering or the details of his conviction; (3) give sufficient particulars as to the identity of said person; (4) give particulars sufficient to identify any covered institution believed to have any information, document, material or object which may be of assistance to the investigation or prosecution; (5) ask from the covered institution concerned any information, document, material or object which may be of assistance to the investigation or prosecution; (6) specify the manner in which and to whom said information, document, material or object obtained pursuant to said request, is to be produced; (7) give all the particulars necessary for the issuance by the court in the requested State of the writs, orders or processes needed by the requesting State; and (8) contain such other information as may assist in the execution of the request.
- Party to key international conventions, including the Vienna Convention, Palermo Convention, and UNCAC
- Member of the Egmont Group and Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG)
column20:

- Organizations and individuals engaged in related non-financial business lines are organizations and individuals that perform one or more of the following activities: provision of prize-winning games, inclyding prize-winning electronic games, games on telecommunications networks or the internet, casinos, lotteries, betting; real estate business, except for real estate leasing, subleasing and real estate consultancy services; trading in precious metals and precious stones; provision of accounting services, notarization services, legal services; provision of services for company establishment, management, and administration; provision of nominee director or company secretary services; provision of legal arrangement services

- there is suspicion that the transaction or the parties involved in the transaction are related to money laundering
- there are doubts about the accuracy or completeness of previously collected customer identification information

- For organizational customers: full name and abbreviated name; head office address; number of establishment license or establishment decision or enterprise registration certificate or equivalent legal document; contact phone number; fax number, website (if any); business and operation sectors; information on founders, legal representatives, Director or General Director, Chief Accountant or person in charge of accounting (if any), including the required information for individuals; information on founders being organizations including name, enterprise registration number or decision on establishment, head office address

- Ensure that the partner bank has performed customer due diligence in accordance with international standards and is able to provide relevant customer information upon request
- Obtain approval from Directors or General Directors or persons authorized by Directors or General Directors for the establishment of correspondent banking relationships
- Cease correspondent banking relationships with shell banks or partner banks that permit their accounts to be used by shell banks
column11:

 (i) is a financial institution or an organization or individual conducting relevant non-financial business lines and professions that has a relationship with the customer, excluding agency or outsourcing relationships;
(ii) conducts customer due diligence in accordance with the provisions of the law or, in the case of a foreign entities, in accordance with the recommendations of FATF
(iii) stores and is ready to provide customer identification information and documents relating to customer due diligence promptly upon request of the reporting entity and ensures confidentiality of such information
(iv) is subject to supervision and inspection by competent authorities

-Where both the third party and its parent company are financial institutions, the reporting entity shall ensure that the third party satisfies the requirements specified in clause 1 of this Article, and the third party's parent company satisfies the requirements concerning identification of customers, politically exposed persons, storage of information, documents, records and reports as specified in Article 9, 17, 38 and 40 of the law or FATF’s relevant recommendations that are applicable to parent companies of financial institutions that are foreign entities, and need to be put to use, as well as monitored in the entire systems of these entities; shall apply risk mitigation policies to sectors at high risks of money laundering.

column17:
- Internal rules and regulations on prevention and combat of money laundering
- Internal audit in AML must include: independent and objective review, inspection, and evaluation of the internal control system, compliance with internal policies and legal provisions on AML; recommendations and proposals to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of AML activities. Internal audit in AML may be carried out independently or combined with other contents but must be a separate section in the audit report. In cases where reporting entities are not required to perform internal audit under the law, reporting entities must ensure compliance monitoring with internal policies and AML law.
- Annually send internal AML audit reports of reporting entities (except reporting entities not required to perform internal audit by law) within 60 days from the end of the fiscal year to the Department of Anti-Money Laundering for reporting entities in the monetary and banking sector; and to ministries or regulatory agencies in charge of respective sectors for other reporting entities. In cases where reporting entities are not required to perform annual internal audit by law, reporting entities shall send reports in accordance with this provision for the audited year.
- Appointment of an AML officer responsible for organizing and implementing activities for prevention and combat of money laundering
- Recruitment and training of personnel specializing in AML activities
- Information technology systems with capability to monitor transactions, detect unusual transactions, and support reporting requirements
column18:

- Reporting of the results of the money laundering risk assessment to SBV and relevant state management agencies within 45 days from the date of completion of the assessment, and dissemination of the same within the reporting entity for implementation
- Assessment and mitigation of money laundering risks that may arise in relation to the development of new products, new business practices, including new delivery mechanisms and the use of new or developing technologies for both new and pre-existing products
column20:

(i) there are any reasonable grounds to suspect that a transaction is on the Blacklist, or it is discovered that parties are related to a transaction on the Blacklist; 
(ii) there are grounds to believe that the requested transaction is related to criminal activity
(iii) requested by competent state authorities in accordance with relevant laws

- Immediate reporting of the transaction postponement measure to SBV and the competent state authority
